title: Microsoft Purview: auto-expanding archive limit rises from 1.5 TB to 3 TB for eligible mailboxes
summary: Hold: the per-user enablement command omits a documented hybrid restriction. Administrators with an on-premises primary mailbox and a cloud archive must enable auto-expanding archiving organisation-wide instead; the capacity increase, eligible licences and automatic arrival are supported.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Cost and licensing; Scope
claims.claim: Eligible Exchange Online archive mailboxes with auto-expanding archiving enabled can grow from 1.5 TB to 3 TB.
claims.quote: Eligible archive mailboxes with auto-expanding archiving enabled can automatically expand beyond the current 1.5 TB limit up to a maximum of 3 TB per mailbox.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes previous expansion support as limited to 1.5 TB, after which mailboxes would become inoperative.
claims.quote: Previously, auto expanding archive mailbox expansion was supported only up to 1.5 TB, after which mailboxes would become inoperative.

claims.claim: The roadmap makes expansion beyond 1.5 TB available to customers with eligible E5 licences.
claims.quote: This capability to expand archive beyond 1.5 TB will be available to customers with eligible E5 licenses.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Governance guidance
claims.claim: The increased ceiling arrives on automatically for eligible mailboxes that already have auto-expanding archiving enabled.
claims.quote: No action is required if eligible mailboxes already have auto-expanding archiving enabled.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The capacity increase is included for mailboxes assigned an eligible licence, including Office 365 E5 or Microsoft 365 E5.
claims.quote:
The increase applies to mailboxes assigned the following eligible licenses:
- Office 365 E5, A5, or G5
- Microsoft 365 E5, A5, or G5

claims.where: What's changing; Why it matters; Cost and licensing; Governance guidance; rationales
claims.claim: Mailboxes without an eligible licence remain limited to 1.5 TB.
claims.quote: For all other licenses, the existing 1.5 TB limit remains unchanged.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; What's changing; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: The change introduces no per-GB consumption charge.
claims.quote: No per-GB consumption charge is introduced as part of this change.

claims.claim: Eligible archive users gain capacity without a support request.
claims.quote: This enhancement helps organizations retain and manage larger volumes of archived email content without requiring manual archive expansion processes or support requests.

claims.claim: Auto-expanding archiving supports a mailbox growth rate that does not exceed 1 GB per day.
claims.quote: Auto-expanding archiving is supported only for mailboxes used by individual users or for shared mailboxes with a growth rate that doesn't exceed 1 GB per day.

claims.claim: eDiscovery tools such as Content Search search the additional storage areas of auto-expanded archives.
claims.quote: When you use an eDiscovery tool, such as Content Search, the additional storage areas in an auto-expanded archive are also searched.

claims.claim: Mailbox holds also cover content in auto-expanded archive storage.
claims.quote: When you put a mailbox on hold by using methods such as Microsoft 365 retention, eDiscovery case holds, and Litigation Hold in Exchange Online, content located in an auto-expanded archive is also placed on hold.

claims.claim: Microsoft describes no new permission or identity for the capacity increase.
claims.quote: Searched: "auto-expanding" "3 TB" permissions identity configuration charge. Opened Learn: Enable auto-expanding archiving, Learn about auto-expanding archiving, Learn about archive mailboxes; read MC1472592. No new permission or identity described.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: A global administrator or member of Organization Management can enable auto-expanding archiving.
claims.quote: To enable auto-expanding archiving, you must be a global administrator in your organization or a member of the Organization Management role group in your Exchange Online organization.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance controls
claims.claim: Membership in a role group containing Mail Recipients is sufficient for enabling auto-expanding archiving for specific users.
claims.quote: Alternately, to enable auto-expanding archiving for specific users, you must be a member of a role group that includes the Mail Recipients role.

claims.where: controls[0].note; controls[1].note; Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Auto-expanding archiving cannot be turned off after it is enabled for an organisation or a user.
claims.quote: After you turn on auto-expanding archiving for your organization or for a specific user, it can't be turned off.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Autonomy & actions; Governance controls
claims.claim: Administrators cannot adjust the storage quota for auto-expanding archiving.
claims.quote: Administrators can't adjust the storage quota for auto-expanding archiving.

claims.quote: For E5 licenses, verify that Records Management is selected and remains enabled in the user's license settings.

claims.claim: Once an archive has an auto-expanded storage area, users cannot delete folders from that archive.
claims.quote: If an archive mailbox has at least one auto-expanded storage area, users can't delete a folder from the archive mailbox or from the auxiliary archive.

claims.claim: Enabling auto-expanding archiving prevents recovering or restoring an inactive mailbox.
claims.quote: Auto-expanding archiving prevents you from recovering or restoring an inactive mailbox.

claims.claim: The cited Learn archive pages state no price for upgrading a user to an eligible licence.
claims.quote: Searched: site:learn.microsoft.com/purview/ "auto-expanding" "3 TB" price license upgrade. Opened Learn: Enable auto-expanding archiving, Learn about auto-expanding archiving, Learn about archive mailboxes. These pages list eligibility and no per-GB charge, not upgrade prices.

claims.claim: Auto-expanding archiving supports shared mailboxes.
claims.quote: Auto-expanding archiving also supports shared mailboxes.

claims.claim: The user's archive mailbox must already be enabled before enabling auto-expanding archiving.
claims.quote: A user's mailbox must already be enabled for archive before you can enable auto-expanding archiving.

claims.claim: Auto-expanding archiving supports cloud-based archive mailboxes in Exchange hybrid deployments.
claims.quote: Auto-expanding archiving is supported for cloud-based archive mailboxes in an Exchange hybrid deployment for users who have an on-premises primary mailbox.

claims.claim: Auto-expanding archiving is not supported for on-premises mailboxes.
claims.quote: Auto-expanding archiving isn't supported for on-premises mailboxes in any version of Exchange Server.

claims.claim: Enabling auto-expanding archiving requires Exchange Online PowerShell rather than the Exchange admin center or Purview portal.
claims.quote: You can't use the Exchange admin center or the Microsoft Purview portal to enable auto-expanding archiving. You must use Exchange Online PowerShell.

claims.claim: There is no documented admin UI path for organisation-wide auto-expanding archiving enablement.
claims.quote: Searched: auto-expanding archiving enable Exchange admin center Purview portal PowerShell hybrid Enable-Mailbox AutoExpandingArchive. Opened Enable auto-expanding archiving: it explicitly rules out both portals and requires Exchange Online PowerShell.

claims.claim: There is no documented admin UI path for per-user auto-expanding archiving enablement.
claims.quote: Searched: auto-expanding archiving enable Exchange admin center Purview portal PowerShell hybrid Enable-Mailbox AutoExpandingArchive. Opened Enable auto-expanding archiving: it explicitly rules out both portals and documents per-user enablement in PowerShell.

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Set-OrganizationConfig -AutoExpandingArchive enables auto-expanding archiving organisation-wide in Exchange Online PowerShell.
claims.quote:
To enable auto-expanding archiving for your entire organization, run the following command:
Set-OrganizationConfig -AutoExpandingArchive

claims.where: controls[1].api; controls[1].note; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Enable-Mailbox <user mailbox> -AutoExpandingArchive is presented as the per-user enablement option without the hybrid restriction.
claims.quote: In an Exchange hybrid deployment, you can't use the Enable-Mailbox -AutoExpandingArchive command to enable auto-expanding archiving for a specific user whose primary mailbox is on-premises and whose archive mailbox is cloud-based.
claims.fix: Keep the call, but append to controls[1].note and the corresponding rendered note: 'This per-user command requires both the primary and archive mailboxes to be cloud-based. For an on-premises primary mailbox with a cloud-based archive, use Set-OrganizationConfig -AutoExpandingArchive in Exchange Online PowerShell to enable auto-expanding archiving for the entire organisation.' Qualify the Before rollout choice of organisation-wide or per-user enablement with the same restriction.

claims.claim: Get-OrganizationConfig | FL AutoExpandingArchiveEnabled checks organisation-wide auto-expanding archiving state.
claims.quote:
To verify that auto-expanding archiving is enabled for your organization, run the following command in Exchange Online PowerShell.
Get-OrganizationConfig | FL AutoExpandingArchiveEnabled

claims.claim: Get-Mailbox <user mailbox> | FL AutoExpandingArchiveEnabled checks a user's auto-expanding archiving property.
claims.quote:
To verify that auto-expanding archiving is enabled for a specific user, run the following command in Exchange Online PowerShell.
Get-Mailbox <user mailbox> | FL AutoExpandingArchiveEnabled

claims.claim: Organisation-wide enablement does not set AutoExpandingArchiveEnabled on individual user mailboxes to True.
claims.quote: Running the Set-OrganizationConfig cmdlet to enable auto-expanding archiving for your organization doesn't change the AutoExpandingArchiveEnabled property on user mailboxes to True.

claims.claim: Per-user enablement for a mailbox on hold or assigned a retention policy increases its primary archive quota by 10 GB.
claims.quote:
When you enable auto-expanding archiving for a specific user and the user's mailbox in on hold or assigned to a retention policy, the following two configurations changes are made:
- The storage quota for the user's primary archive mailbox is increased by 10 GB (from 100 GB to 110 GB).

claims.claim: The Learn overview body still describes a 1.5 TB maximum despite its notice of the increase.
claims.quote: This archiving feature in Microsoft Purview (called auto-expanding archiving) provides up to 1.5 TB of additional storage in archive mailboxes.

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn's archive pages carry the capacity-increase notice.
claims.quote: Microsoft is increasing the maximum auto-expanding archive capacity for eligible Exchange Online mailboxes from 1.5 TB to 3 TB. Rollout begins in mid-October 2026 and is expected to complete by late October.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft recommends reviewing licence assignments for users with large archives.
claims.quote: Review license assignments for users with large archive mailboxes to confirm eligibility.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends monitoring archive growth using Exchange Online PowerShell.
claims.quote: Monitor archive mailbox growth using Exchange Online PowerShell.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft recommends updating documentation, retention guidance and help desk materials for the new limit.
claims.quote: Update internal documentation, retention guidance, and help desk materials to reflect the new 3 TB limit.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft recommends reviewing licensing and retention strategies for users ineligible for expanded capacity.
claims.quote: Review licensing and retention strategies for users whose archive mailboxes are not eligible for the expanded capacity.

claims.claim: Microsoft recommends identifying mailboxes approaching their applicable capacity limit.
claims.quote: Identify mailboxes approaching their applicable archive capacity limits.

claims.claim: The sources for this change do not establish rollout timing for other clouds despite listing G5 and GOV licences.
claims.quote: Searched: "auto-expanding" "3 TB" GCC government rollout. Read roadmap, MC1472592 and the three cited Learn archive pages. Worldwide timing and G5/GOV eligibility are stated; separate rollout timing for other clouds is not.

claims.claim: The pages for this change do not state what happens to an archive exceeding 1.5 TB if its eligible licence is removed.
claims.quote: Searched: "auto-expanding" "3 TB" "removed" license; auto expanding archive 3 TB shared mailbox eligible license removed downgrade 1.5 TB. Opened all three cited Learn archive pages and read MC1472592; no treatment of an already-over-limit archive after licence removal is stated.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls table
claims.claim: The checklist asks administrators to check Records Management in licence settings, but neither controls-table row covers that setting.
claims.quote: Verify that Records Management is selected and enabled in the licence settings of E5 users, as Learn instructs. / Auto-expanding archiving for the whole organisation / Auto-expanding archiving for specific users
claims.fix: Remove the Records Management verification bullet from the Before rollout checklist; retain the verified licensing prerequisite under Risk assessment. This removes the checklist/table mismatch without adding an unverified control path.

controlChecks.governs: Auto-expanding archiving for the whole organisation
